sanskrit: tasmān na dviṣann adyān na dviṣato 'nnam adyān na mīmāṃsitasya na mīmāṃsyamānasya ||
english: Therefore one should not eat while harbouring hatred, nor should one eat the food of one who harbours hatred; nor the food of one who is under suspicion, nor of one who is being questioned with suspicion.

sanskrit: sarvo vā eṣo jagdhapāpmā yasyānnam aśnanti ||
english: He whose food others eat is one whose sin has been consumed — he is wholly freed of evil.

sanskrit: sarva u eṣo 'jagdhapāpmā yasyānnaṃ nāśnanti ||
english: He whose food others do not eat is one whose sin has not been consumed — he is wholly burdened with evil.

sanskrit: prajāpater vā eṣa vikrāntam anuvikrame ya upaharanti ||
english: Those who present the offering follow in the stride of Prajāpati's own great stride.

sanskrit: prajāpatyo vā etasyaiva yajño vitato ya upaharati ||
english: The sacrifice spread forth by him who presents the offering is indeed the sacrifice belonging to Prajāpati.

sanskrit: sarvadā vā eṣa sutasomo yuktagrāvārdrapavitra āhṛtayajñakratur vitatādhavaro ya upaharati ||
english: He who presents the offering is at all times one for whom the soma has been pressed, the pressing-stones are yoked, the strainer is moist, the rite of the sacrifice has been performed, and the adhvara has been spread.

sanskrit: yo 'tithīnāṃ sa āhavanīyo yo 'nnakaraṇaḥ sa dakṣiṇāgnir yo veśmani sa gārhapatyaḥ ||
english: He who is for the guests is the āhavanīya fire; he who is the preparer of food is the dakṣiṇāgni; he who abides in the household is the gārhapatya.

sanskrit: iṣṭaṃ ca vā eṣa pūrtaṃ cāśnāti yaḥ pūrvo 'tither aśnāti ||
english: He who eats before the guest eats up both the iṣṭa — the fruit of sacrificial rites — and the pūrta — the fruit of works of public merit.

sanskrit: prajāṃ ca vā eṣa paśūṃś cāśnāti (…) ||
english: He likewise eats away his progeny and his cattle — [he who eats before the guest].

sanskrit: ūrjaṃ ca vā eṣa payaś ca gṛhāṇām aśnāti yaḥ pūrvo 'tither aśnāti ||
english: He who eats before the guest eats away the vigour and the milk-wealth of the households.

sanskrit: eṣa vā atithir yac chrotriyaḥ ||
english: He who is a learned Vedic scholar — he indeed is the true atithi, the guest.

sanskrit: tasmāt pūrvo nāśnīyād aśitāvaty aśnīyāt tad vratam ||
english: Therefore one should not eat first; one should eat only after he has eaten — that is the vow, the sacred rule.

sanskrit: yajñasyāvicchedāya yajñasya guptaye yajñasya sātmatvāya ||
english: For the unbroken continuity of the sacrifice, for the protection of the sacrifice, for the sacrifice's identification with the self.

sanskrit: yat kṣīram upasicyopaharati yāvad agniṣṭomea samṛddheneṣṭvāvarundhe tāvad enenāva rundhe ||
english: When one presents the offering with milk poured over it, one thereby obtains as much merit as is obtained by sacrificing with a fully performed Agniṣṭoma — so much does one secure through this.

sanskrit: yat sarpir upasicyopaharati yāvat sāhnena samṛddhena (…) ||
english: When one presents the offering with clarified butter poured over it, one thereby obtains as much as is obtained by a fully performed sāhna sacrifice — [so much does one secure through this].

sanskrit: yan madhūpasicyopaharati yāvad atirātreṇa samṛddhena (…) ||
english: When one presents the offering with honey poured over it, one thereby obtains as much as is obtained by a fully performed atirātra sacrifice — [so much does one secure through this].

sanskrit: yan māṃsam upasicyopaharati yāvad dvādaśāhnena samṛddheneṣṭvāvarundhe tāvad enenāva rundhe ||
english: When one presents the offering with meat poured over it, one thereby obtains as much merit as is obtained by sacrificing with a fully performed dvādaśāhna — so much does one secure through this.

sanskrit: yad udakam upasicyopaharati prajānāṃ prajananāya jyog jīvati sarvam āyur eti na punar ā jarasaḥ pramīyate ya evaṃ veda ||
english: When one presents the offering with water poured over it, it is for the procreation of progeny; he lives long, he attains the full span of life, and he does not die before old age — he who knows thus.

sanskrit: tasmai vāta uṣā hiṅ kṛṇoti savitā bhūtyā pra stauti bṛhaspatir ūrjayodgāyati tvaṣṭā puṣṭyā prati harati viśve devā nidhanam | nidhanaṃ bhūtyāḥ prajāyāḥ paśūnāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: For him, Vāta and Uṣas intone the hiṅkāra; Savitṛ extols him with prosperity as the prastāva; Bṛhaspati chants the udgītha with vigour; Tvaṣṭṛ performs the pratihāra with nourishment; the Viśve Devāḥ perform the nidhana. The nidhana becomes one of prosperity, of progeny, and of cattle — for him who knows thus.

sanskrit: tasmā udyant sūryo hiṅkṛṇoti saṃgavaḥ pra stauti madhyandina udgāyaty aparāhṇaḥ prati haraty astaṃyan nidhanam | (…) ||
english: For him, the rising sun intones the hiṅkāra; the forenoon performs the prastāva; the midday chants the udgītha; the afternoon performs the pratihāra; the setting sun performs the nidhana — [and the nidhana becomes one of prosperity, of progeny, and of cattle, for him who knows thus].

sanskrit: tasmā abhro bhavan hiṅ kṛṇoti vidyotamānaḥ pra stauti stanayann udgāyati varṣan prati haraty udgṛhṇan nidhanam | (…) ||
english: For him, the forming cloud intones the hiṅkāra; the lightning flashing forth performs the prastāva; the thundering chants the udgītha; the raining performs the pratihāra; the clearing performs the nidhana — [and the nidhana becomes one of prosperity, of progeny, and of cattle, for him who knows thus].

sanskrit: atithīn prati paśyati hiṅ kṛṇoty abhi vadati pra stauty udakaṃ yācaty udgāyaty upa harati prati haraty ucchiṣṭaṃ nidhanam | nidhanaṃ bhūtyāḥ prajāyāḥ paśūnāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: He looks towards the guests — that is the hiṅkāra; he addresses them with welcome — that is the prastāva; he requests water — that is the udgītha; he brings the offering forward — that is the pratihāra; he performs the nidhana with the remnant. The nidhana becomes one of prosperity, of progeny, and of cattle — for him who knows thus.
